english.notes:
(i) Section 94A(2) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 provides that section 88 (exceptions to driving licences) of the Act shall apply in relation to section 94A(1) as it applies in relation to section 87 of the Act (motor vehicle driving licence offences).
(ii) This offence should be considered for offenders whose DVLA record shows their licence is 'Revoked / Refused - Medical'. This is when DVLA have been notified of a reason why the person may not be safe to drive, such as a medical condition or persistent drug misuse. The potential danger to the public presented by this offender is increased, hence why the potential penalty is imprisonable, akin to disqualified driving.
(iii) This offence should not be used where an offender's licence has been revoked under the Road Traffic (New Drivers) Act 1995. Where this is the case, the offence in document H9420 (CJS code RT88334) should be considered.

Six months imprisonment and / or fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Discretionary disqualification

6 months
